questionsAndDecisions.source: Human architect confirmation in the active AI interaction
questionsAndDecisions.answer: All production data, backups, logs, model inputs and outputs, and routine processing must remain within approved EU/EEA locations. Transfers outside the EEA are prohibited unless the General Counsel and Data Protection Officer approve a documented legal mechanism, purpose, and risk assessment. Privileged administration and operational access must use Stratton-controlled identities and be limited to authorised EU-based personnel, with least privilege, time-bound elevation, complete auditability, and an approved emergency-access process. Contracts, data processing, incident handling, and dispute governance must remain subject to applicable EU and member-state law, with any foreign-jurisdiction exposure explicitly assessed and accepted. The General Counsel is accountable for final confirmation, advised by the DPO and CISO.
questionsAndDecisions.rationale: This defines the mandatory sovereignty outcomes, controlled exception path, privileged-access conditions, jurisdictional governance and accountable confirmation authority without selecting an architecture or service.
questionsAndDecisions.followUp: Obtain the General Counsel's final confirmation and retain the documented decision; define approved EU/EEA locations, exception evidence and operational procedures before baselining dependent requirements.

questionsAndDecisions.question: For the first-release due-diligence workflow, which authoritative source systems and data classes may be used, who owns each, and what classification, personal-data, retention, quality, licensing or permitted-use constraints apply?
questionsAndDecisions.rationale: The outcome and sovereignty boundary are now confirmed, but the platform cannot establish lawful, safe or testable ingestion and AI-processing requirements until its governed inputs and accountable owners are known.

questionsAndDecisions.source: Human architect confirmation in the active AI interaction
questionsAndDecisions.answer: Release 1 may use governed deal-room and document-management records owned by Deal Operations; deal pipeline and CRM records owned by Investment Origination; portfolio and financial records owned by Finance; ESG submissions owned by the ESG function; and legal and compliance records owned by General Counsel and Compliance. External market, company, patent, sanctions, and regulatory data may be used only where licensing explicitly permits AI-assisted retrieval and analysis. Deal, financial, legal, and portfolio data is highly confidential. Personal data must be minimised, and special-category data is excluded unless separately approved. Every item must retain source provenance, owner, timestamp, licence, and quality status. Stratton data must not train foundation models, and AI outputs require human validation before investment use. Retention follows the authoritative source-system schedule and legal holds; temporary AI working copies are deleted when no longer required.
questionsAndDecisions.rationale: This establishes the permitted source domains and accountable owners, external-data licence gate, core classification and privacy constraints, provenance and quality metadata, model-training prohibition, human-validation rule, and retention and deletion boundaries for Release 1.
questionsAndDecisions.followUp: Identify exact authoritative systems and schedules, define quality thresholds and volumes, and obtain any separately required approval before special-category data enters scope.

questionsAndDecisions.question: Within Release 1 due diligence, which tasks and decisions may AI perform or support, which named human roles must review or approve each material output, and which actions are prohibited from autonomous execution?

recommendation.proposal: Limit AI to evidence retrieval, extraction, summarisation, comparison, anomaly flagging and draft risk-assessment support; require an assigned deal professional to validate cited evidence and conclusions, with the Investment Committee retaining the investment decision; prohibit autonomous recommendations being treated as final, source alteration, external disclosure, transaction execution, or bypass of legal, compliance and conflicts review.

Existing deal, legal, compliance and conflicts approvals remain authoritative.

questionsAndDecisions.source: Human architect confirmation in the active AI interaction
questionsAndDecisions.answer: Release 1 AI may perform retrieval, extraction, summarisation, comparison, anomaly flagging, and draft risk assessments. Deal professionals must validate source evidence and material outputs. General Counsel and Compliance must approve regulated, legal, sanctions, or externally sourced conclusions. The Investment Committee retains every investment decision. AI must not autonomously issue final investment recommendations, alter authoritative sources, disclose information externally, execute transactions, make approval decisions, or bypass required legal, compliance, security, or human review. The Head of AI Governance owns AI policy and model-risk controls, while the Chief Investment Officer is accountable for business-output acceptance.

questionsAndDecisions.question: What measurable acceptance thresholds and evidence must Release 1 meet for source citation, extraction accuracy, unsupported claims, risk-assessment quality, prohibited-action prevention, human-review completion, and the 3-week business outcome?

recommendation.proposal: Require every material AI claim to cite an accessible governed source; test extraction and risk outputs against an approved representative benchmark with thresholds set by the Head of AI Governance and Chief Investment Officer; allow no critical prohibited-action or external-disclosure breach; evidence every required human approval in an immutable audit trail; and measure the 3-week outcome from workflow timestamps, with mocked evidence labelled synthetic and excluded from claims of achieved production benefit.
assumptions: A representative, lawfully usable benchmark set can be assembled before acceptance testing.
The workflow can produce reliable case-opening, review, approval and investment-committee-readiness timestamps.
Release 1 acceptance can distinguish technical AI quality from later production benefit realisation.

questionsAndDecisions.source: Human architect confirmation in the active AI interaction
questionsAndDecisions.answer: Release 1 requires governed source citations for 100% of material claims; at least 95% field-level extraction accuracy and 99% accuracy for critical financial and legal fields on an approved representative benchmark; zero critical unsupported claims and no more than 2% unsupported non-critical claims; at least 90% recall for seeded high-risk findings with no critical risk missed; 100% prevention of prohibited actions in negative testing; and auditable human review for every material output. The 3-week outcome is measured from workflow timestamps across the first 20 eligible completed deals, with control exceptions tracked to ensure cycle-time improvement does not reduce quality. Synthetic or mocked evidence is clearly labelled and excluded from production-benefit claims. The Head of AI Governance owns benchmark data, Model Risk or Internal Audit owns independent validation, General Counsel and Compliance accept regulated tests, and the Chief Investment Officer accepts the business-benefit evidence.
questionsAndDecisions.rationale: This makes the AI quality, safety, human-review and business-benefit outcomes measurable, assigns acceptance responsibilities, and prevents synthetic evidence from being represented as achieved production benefit.

questionsAndDecisions.followUp: Assign either Model Risk or Internal Audit as the accountable independent validator and define benchmark eligibility, critical-field classification, unsupported-claim severity, eligible-deal criteria and control-exception handling before baselining acceptance tests.

questionsAndDecisions.source: Human architect confirmation in the active AI interaction
questionsAndDecisions.answer: Existing deal-room, CRM, finance, ESG, and legal systems remain authoritative. Release 1 integrates through approved read-only APIs or controlled ingestion and must not write AI-generated content into source records. Development, test, and production environments are separated; development and test use synthetic data, while production-confidential data remains only in production. Production targets 99.9% availability during business hours, RTO of 4 hours, RPO of 1 hour, p95 interactive response below 5 seconds, and processing of a typical due-diligence document pack within 30 minutes. Migration is incremental with reconciliation and parallel operation for the first three eligible deals; no big-bang replacement is permitted. Support is 8x5 with monitored critical alerts and named incident ownership. Enterprise Platform owns environments, the Integration Lead owns interfaces, Identity and Network leads own access and connectivity, Service Operations owns support, Business Continuity owns recovery, and Programme Delivery owns migration.
questionsAndDecisions.rationale: This confirms the system-of-record boundary, permitted integration modes, environment and data separation, measurable service targets, incremental migration safeguards, support model and accountable technology and operations owners.
rejectedAlternatives: AI-generated write-back to authoritative source records in Release 1
questionsAndDecisions.followUp: Define business hours, typical document-pack characteristics, critical-alert criteria and the evidence method for availability, recovery, performance, reconciliation and parallel-operation acceptance.

questionsAndDecisions.source: Human architect confirmation in the active AI interaction
questionsAndDecisions.answer: GDPR applies because Release 1 processes EU personal data; it requires data minimisation, purpose limitation, documented lawful basis, data-subject handling, DPIA screening, processor controls, and transfer governance, confirmed by the DPO and General Counsel. SFDR applies where ESG outputs support regulated disclosures; it requires data lineage, quality, reproducibility, accountable review, and audit evidence, confirmed by the Head of Compliance. AIFMD applies where Luxembourg AIF vehicles use the workflow; it requires governed risk and documentation records and applicable retention, confirmed by Fund Legal and Compliance. The EU AI Act applies as an AI governance framework, but Release 1 is not classified as high-risk unless a documented role and use-case assessment concludes otherwise; AI literacy, transparency, human oversight, logging, risk management, and classification evidence are required, confirmed by General Counsel and the Head of AI Governance. DORA remains a candidate requiring General Counsel confirmation because the cloud and AI service may support a regulated financial entity; ICT resilience, incident, testing, and third-party obligations must be assessed. The unspecified sector directives are removed unless Legal identifies exact instruments and triggers. General Counsel owns final applicability decisions.
questionsAndDecisions.rationale: This confirms applicability, material constraints and accountable authorities for GDPR, SFDR, AIFMD and the EU AI Act; retains DORA as an explicitly owned candidate; and removes the unsupported generic sector-directive lead unless Legal supplies an exact instrument and trigger.
rejectedAlternatives: Treating the unspecified sector-specific directives as applicable without identified instruments and triggers
Classifying Release 1 as EU AI Act high-risk without a documented role and use-case assessment
questionsAndDecisions.followUp: AFF-0 must append an evidence-backed regulatory-register revision reflecting the confirmed entries, removed generic lead and open DORA candidate. General Counsel must complete the DORA assessment and retain the AI Act role and use-case classification evidence.

questionsAndDecisions.answer: Release 1 is a controlled production rollout for the first 20 eligible new private-equity investment opportunities handled by Stratton deal teams, Legal and Compliance reviewers, AI Governance, and Investment Committee members. It includes governed evidence ingestion, retrieval, extraction, comparison, risk and ESG analysis, source citations, human review, and preparation of an investment-committee-ready draft recommendation. Deals across Stratton's stated Central European footprint are eligible only where all processing satisfies the confirmed sovereignty rules. Release 1 excludes portfolio-company monitoring, automated SFDR filing, deal-sourcing automation, autonomous decisions or transactions, external counterparty communications, source-system write-back or replacement, special-category data, and wider production rollout until acceptance criteria pass. The Chief Investment Officer is product sponsor, Head of Deal Operations owns deal eligibility, General Counsel owns jurisdiction eligibility, Programme Delivery owns rollout, and the relevant business owners accept deferred capabilities.
